summary: Reject colliding reassigns at queue time instead of at apply
description:
`POST /api/tags/:id/action` validates only the request *shape*. The zod schema
checks that a `reassign` carries a non-empty `reassign_to` string and nothing
else, so the API will happily queue a reassign that cannot possibly apply.

The collision it misses: if the target concept already has a `pending`
staged_tag on the same chunk at the same `(model, prompt_version)`, the insert
in `insertReassignedTag` violates `idx_staged_tags_provenance_unique`. Because
`buildApply` drains the whole queue inside one `rw.transaction`, that raise
rolls back **every other verdict in the batch** — a 2,579-action review pass
discarded by one bad row.

## Why a 409 at queue time

`scripts/validate_queue.py` (added 2026-08-09) catches this before apply, but
it is a net under a hole. Refusing the action at queue time makes the bad state
unreachable rather than merely detectable, and gives the reviewer the error at
the moment they can still pick a different donor or target.

Suggested shape: on `action === 'reassign'`, look up pending tags for
`(chunk_id, reassign_to, model, prompt_version)` and return 409 with the
colliding staged_tag id. The lookup is the same one validate_queue.py does.

## Ordering subtlety worth encoding in the check

The queue applies `ORDER BY ra.id DESC` — reverse insertion order. So a reject
that would clear the target concept out of the way only helps if it was queued
*after* the reassign. A naive queue-time check that just asks "is the target
pending right now?" will produce false positives for that legitimate pattern,
and false negatives if an earlier-queued reject is assumed to clear the way.
See `test_clearing_reject_must_be_queued_after_the_reassign` in
tests/test_validate_queue.py for both directions.

## Related

- Mechanism and caveats: docs/ingest/11-tag-review.md, Failure modes.
- The partial index (`WHERE status = 'pending'`) is what makes the donor's own
  row safe; only a *different* pending row can collide.

analysis.author: Hermes Agent
analysis.content:
Blocked on todo:7a815c05, found while implementing this.

This ticket's "Ordering subtlety worth encoding in the check" section is built on validate_queue.py's claim that the queue applies ORDER BY ra.id DESC. It does not. buildApply drains selectQueuedActions (ORDER BY id ASC) and iterates it directly; the DESC ordering belongs to selectQueueWithContext, which only feeds the queue display route.

Proven in guru-review/server/src/apply.test.ts ('queue drain order') against the real openDb / buildApply: reject-then-reassign applies clean; reassign-then-reject throws UNIQUE constraint failed. Exactly the reverse of what this ticket and tests/test_validate_queue.py assume.

Two consequences for the design here:

1. The suggested check — look up pending tags for (chunk_id, reassign_to, model, prompt_version) and return 409 — is not sufficient. Under insertion order a newly queued action gets the highest id and so applies LAST, meaning every already-queued action applies before it. The check has to replay the existing queue rather than inspect current state, or it will 409 on a queue an earlier reject would have cleared.

2. The false-positive worry inverts too. Under insertion order the working reviewer flow is the intuitive one — reject the occupant, then reassign onto the freed concept — so a queue-time 409 does not block anything a reviewer would naturally do. That makes the 409 a better idea than this ticket feared, once computed against a correct replay.

Not attempted rather than shipped half-correct: a 409 built on the inverted model would reject valid queues and pass the batch-destroying one.
